briefdescription.para: Dispatch map that reports engine events to Processor and StopManager.

detaileddescription.para: Both register their handlers in their constructors. The session fires an event with events.get, on the engine context.

briefdescription.para: The liblldb debugger instance owning target and process for this session's lifetime.
Listens for process, target, and breakpoint events; polled by pollEvents.
The debug target created by launch or attach.
The debuggee process bound to target once launch or attach succeeds.
Variable list for the frame identified by cachedFrameIndex, rebuilt by cacheFrameVariables when the requested frame index changes.
Frame index cachedFrameVariables was built for, or -1 when no cache is valid.
Creates a session with no engine objects.

detaileddescription.para: initialize creates them.

briefdescription.para: Calls shutdown with EndMode::passive.
Prepare the debug engine for use.

detaileddescription.para: Must succeed before any other Session method.

Windows: CoInitializeEx (multithreaded), loads dbgeng.dll from sidecarDir via Loader, calls DebugCreate to obtain IDebugClient5, QueryInterface for IDebugControl4/IDebugSymbols3/IDebugDataSpaces4/IDebugSystemObjects, registers OutputCallbacks and EventCallbacks, sets source-level code level for stepping, and enables the initial-break engine option. On failure it calls shutdown(EndMode::passive).

macOS: SBDebugger::Initialize/Create (async mode), redirects the debugger's own stdin to /dev/null so liblldb does not compete with the DAP reader thread for whatdbg's stdin, and captures the SBListener.

parameterdescription.para: Directory containing extracted dbgeng sidecar DLLs. Unused on macOS.

simplesect.para: true if the engine is ready for launch/attach.
Called on the engine context, by Processor::onPrepare.

briefdescription.para: Launch a process for debugging, stopped before user code runs.

detaileddescription.para: Windows calls IDebugClient5::CreateProcess2 and returns immediately — it does NOT call WaitForEvent, so the caller must poll via pollEvents() to receive the initial CreateProcess and loader-breakpoint events.

macOS creates the target, starts listening for its events, then calls SBTarget::Launch with eLaunchFlagDebug | eLaunchFlagStopAtEntry. On success the target and process members are populated, and the session fires the targetProcessId event. The caller still polls via pollEvents() for the resulting stop event.

parameterdescription.para: Full path to the executable to launch.

simplesect.para: true if the launch call succeeded.
The process is stopped before running any code until the first pollEvents call.

briefdescription.para: Attach to a running process by OS process ID.

detaileddescription.para: Windows calls IDebugClient5::AttachProcess and returns immediately — it does NOT call WaitForEvent, so the caller must poll via pollEvents() to receive the initial attach-break event.
macOS creates an empty target, starts listening for its events, then calls SBTarget::AttachToProcessWithID. Processor::onAttach stores the target process id after this call returns true.

parameterdescription.para: OS process ID of the target process.

simplesect.para: true if the attach call succeeded.

briefdescription.para: Resume execution after a break.

detaileddescription.para: Windows calls IDebugControl4::SetExecutionStatus(DEBUG_STATUS_GO). macOS calls SBProcess::Continue.

briefdescription.para: Poll for debug events with a timeout.

detaileddescription.para: Processor::process calls it on the engine context while the target runs or launches, or while a terminate deadline is pending. Windows calls IDebugControl4::WaitForEvent with timeoutMs. dbgeng invokes the callbacks in Callbacks.cpp during that call. Afterwards, E_UNEXPECTED from the wait fires the terminated event, and S_OK with a step pending fires the step event. macOS calls SBListener::WaitForEvent, which only accepts whole-second timeouts, so timeoutMs is rounded up to the next second before the wait. Each timeoutMs from 1 to 1000 waits one second. A process event goes to the stop-reason dispatch. A breakpoint event of type LocationsAdded or LocationsResolved fires breakpointLocationFound.

parameterdescription.para: Maximum time to wait in milliseconds. On macOS, 0 is a non-blocking poll.

briefdescription.para: Detach from the target and release all engine resources.

detaileddescription.para: Safe to call more than once. Processor::onReleaseResources, initialize on failure (Windows), and ~Session call it. On Windows a second call finds client null and skips EndSession. On macOS a second call finds the debugger invalid and does nothing.

mode
How to end the session:
EndMode::terminate — target is alive; kill it on detach
EndMode::detach — target is alive; leave it running after detach
EndMode::passive — target has already exited; release state only
Windows calls IDebugClient5::EndSession with the dbgeng flag corresponding to mode, unregisters OutputCallbacks and EventCallbacks, releases all COM interface pointers, and calls CoUninitialize if this Session owns the COM apartment. macOS signals or detaches the process per mode, then destroys and terminates the SBDebugger.

simplesect.para: Callers must pass an explicit mode. The destructor passes EndMode::passive. Processor::getEndModeForExit returns EndMode::passive when the target has exited.

briefdescription.para: Wakes a blocked pollEvents.

detaileddescription.para: Called on the reader thread, from Processor::addRequest.
macOS broadcasts the wake event on the listener. Windows does nothing.

briefdescription.para: Requests interruption of the engine wait.

detaileddescription.para: Called on the reader thread, for disconnect and terminate requests.
Windows calls IDebugControl4::SetInterrupt with DEBUG_INTERRUPT_EXIT. macOS calls wake.

briefdescription.para: Called on the engine context when a disconnect or terminate request starts.

detaileddescription.para: Windows calls IDebugControl4::GetInterrupt. macOS does nothing.

briefdescription.para: Resolve a source file path and line number to a resolution status.

detaileddescription.para: Windows calls IDebugSymbols3::GetOffsetByLine, first against the full path, then against the basename with a stored-path match. It distinguishes a transient engine error (E_UNEXPECTED, engineBusy) from a genuine miss.
macOS searches every compile unit of every loaded module for a matching line entry (FindLineEntryIndex); liblldb has no transient-busy signal, so this side never returns engineBusy.

parameterdescription.para: Path to the source file (backslash-form on Windows, forward-slash on macOS).
One-based source line number.

simplesect.para: OffsetStatus::found — symbol found; getOffset() returns the address. OffsetStatus::notFound — no code at this line or module not loaded. OffsetStatus::engineBusy — Windows only: engine transient error; retry later.

briefdescription.para: Resolve a source file path and line number to a target virtual address.

detaileddescription.para: Windows performs the same lookup as getOffsetStatus and returns the resolved offset. macOS performs the same compile-unit search as getOffsetStatus and returns SBLineEntry::GetStartAddress resolved to a load address via the target.

parameterdescription.para: Path to the source file (backslash-form on Windows, forward-slash on macOS).
One-based source line number.

simplesect.para: Resolved virtual address, or 0 when there is none.

briefdescription.para: Create a code breakpoint at the given virtual address.

detaileddescription.para: Windows calls IDebugControl4::AddBreakpoint2 and enables the resulting breakpoint. macOS calls SBTarget::BreakpointCreateByAddress. Both return the engine-assigned breakpoint ID, used for subsequent removeBreakpoint calls and to match incoming breakpoint-hit notifications.

parameterdescription.para: Virtual address at which to set the breakpoint.

simplesect.para: The engine-assigned breakpoint ID, or an empty optional when creation fails.

briefdescription.para: Create a breakpoint by source file and line.

detaileddescription.para: Cross-platform entry: Windows wraps the existing getOffsetStatus / getOffset → addBreakpoint (offset) chain; macOS delegates to SBTarget::BreakpointCreateByLocation, which lets liblldb track pending locations itself and auto-resolve as modules load (no adapter-side retry loop).

parameterdescription.para: Source file path, in the path form the target platform expects (backslash-form on Windows, forward-slash on macOS).
Requested line (1-based, matching DAP).

simplesect.para: BreakpointLocation packing (engineId, resolvedLine), or an empty optional when no location was found or BP creation failed. On macOS resolvedLine is 0 when the BP has no location yet; the caller then treats it as pending, and liblldb resolves it later.

briefdescription.para: Remove a previously created breakpoint by its engine ID.

detaileddescription.para: Windows calls IDebugControl4::GetBreakpointById2 then RemoveBreakpoint2 and fails explicitly if the ID is not found. macOS calls SBTarget::BreakpointDelete, which reports the same not-found case as a plain false. The engine ID is no longer valid after a successful removal.

parameterdescription.para: The engine-assigned breakpoint ID returned by addBreakpoint.

simplesect.para: juce::Result::ok() on success, or juce::Result::fail(...) if the ID is not found.

briefdescription.para: Force-reload symbols for a specific module.

detaileddescription.para: Windows executes ".reload /f" with the basename of imageName, via IDebugControl4::Execute. BreakpointManager::onModuleLoad calls it after a module loads. macOS is a no-op. liblldb loads a module's symbols during module-load handling, so this always returns ok().

parameterdescription.para: The image file name (basename or full path) as reported by the moduleLoad event. Unused on macOS.

simplesect.para: juce::Result::ok() if the reload executed without error, or always on macOS.

briefdescription.para: Force-reload symbols for all currently loaded modules.

detaileddescription.para: Windows executes ".reload /f" with no module name, via IDebugControl4::Execute. BreakpointManager::onReload calls it. macOS is a no-op for the same reason as loadModuleSymbols and always returns ok().

simplesect.para: juce::Result::ok() if the reload executed without error, or always on macOS.

briefdescription.para: Step over one source line without entering function calls.

detaileddescription.para: Windows calls IDebugControl4::SetExecutionStatus(DEBUG_STATUS_STEP_OVER); requires source-level code level, set during initialize. macOS calls SBThread::StepOver(eOnlyDuringStepping) on the selected thread.

simplesect.para: The step completes asynchronously. Windows fires the step event from pollEvents when a wait returns S_OK with a step pending. macOS fires it from the stop-reason dispatch.

briefdescription.para: Step into the next function call on the current source line.

detaileddescription.para: Windows calls IDebugControl4::SetExecutionStatus(DEBUG_STATUS_STEP_INTO); requires source-level code level, set during initialize. macOS calls SBThread::StepInto on the selected thread.

simplesect.para: The step completes asynchronously, as described for stepOver.

briefdescription.para: Step out of the current function to its call site.

detaileddescription.para: Windows executes the "gu" (go up) command via IDebugControl4::Execute. macOS calls SBThread::StepOutOfFrame on the thread's selected frame.

simplesect.para: The step completes asynchronously, as described for stepOver.

briefdescription.para: Interrupt a running target process.

detaileddescription.para: Windows opens the process with PROCESS_VM_OPERATION, PROCESS_VM_WRITE, and PROCESS_CREATE_THREAD, then calls DebugBreakProcess on it. macOS calls SBProcess::SendAsyncInterrupt on the already-bound process; processId is unused there since the Session already knows its target. The resulting break is reported as a normal stop event.

parameterdescription.para: OS process ID of the target to interrupt. Unused on macOS.

briefdescription.para: Request debuggee termination without blocking the caller.

detaileddescription.para: Sends a kill request to the target process and returns immediately. The exit is observed later through pollEvents. Processor handles the exited and terminated events. Windows calls IDebugClient5::TerminateProcesses, which targets the process this client is already debugging. macOS sends SIGKILL via SBProcess::Signal and, on success, resumes the process so it can act on the pending signal and exit. If Signal fails, it falls back to SBProcess::Kill, which asks LLDB to terminate the process directly.

parameterdescription.para: OS process ID of the target to terminate. Unused on both platforms. The session already knows its bound process.

simplesect.para: Callers must keep polling until the exit is observed. Processor::process keeps polling while terminateDeadlineMs is set.

briefdescription.para: Append a path to the symbol search path.

detaileddescription.para: Windows calls IDebugSymbols3::AppendSymbolPath — the appended path is searched in addition to any path set at initialization time. macOS runs the LLDB command "settings append target.debug-file-search-paths <path>" via HandleCommand, which is likewise additive.

parameterdescription.para: Semicolon-delimited symbol path to append (e.g. "C:\\Symbols;srv*") on Windows; a single filesystem path on macOS.

briefdescription.para: Append a path to the source search path.

detaileddescription.para: Windows calls IDebugSymbols3::AppendSourcePath, which is additive. macOS has no additive source search path — it runs the LLDB command "settings set target.source-map \".\" \"<path>\"", which remaps "." to path and replaces the full source map on every call; current callers invoke it once.

parameterdescription.para: Semicolon-delimited source path to append on Windows; a single filesystem path to remap "." to on macOS.

memberdef.argsstring: (std::string &json, int maxFrames, const std::function< int(int frameIndex)> &addFrame) noexcept
memberdef.name: appendStackFrames

briefdescription.para: Appends the stack frames of the current thread to json, as DAP stack frame objects.

detaileddescription.para: Windows walks the call stack up to maxFrames deep using IDebugControl4::GetStackTrace and resolves each frame to source file, line, and function name via IDebugSymbols3::GetNameByOffset and GetLineByOffset. macOS reads SBThread::GetNumFrames and each SBFrame's function name and SBLineEntry directly, clamped to the real stack depth.
addFrame is called once for each frame, in frame order. Its return value is the id that the frame object carries. VariableManager assigns the ids.

Each appended frame object has these fields:
id (int) — the value that addFrame returned for the frame
name (String) — function name, or "frame" (Windows) or "??" (macOS) when unavailable
source (Object) — { name, path }; present only when line information is available
line (int) — one-based source line number; present only with source
column (int) — always 1; present only with source

parameterdescription.para: Output text that receives the frame objects.
Maximum number of frames to request. Windows requests maxFrames frames and appends those that GetStackTrace fills. macOS appends at most the stack depth.
Called with the frame index. Returns the DAP id of the frame.

simplesect.para: Number of frame objects appended.
Must be called while the target is stopped.

memberdef.name: applyToLocals

param.type: const std::function< void(const juce::String &name, const juce::String &value, const juce::String &type, bool hasChildren, int symbolIndex)> &

briefdescription.para: Calls function for each local variable of a stack frame, in symbol order.

detaileddescription.para: Windows iterates the top-level symbols of the frame's symbol group, obtained through getOrCreateSymbolGroup. Value formatting uses debug::prettyPrint and debug::formatSymbolValue. macOS iterates SBFrame::GetVariables, cached by cacheFrameVariables. Value formatting uses the macOS debug::prettyPrint overload. Both sides skip the names that shouldSkipSymbol matches.
function receives the symbol name, the formatted value, the type name, whether the symbol has children, and the symbol index in the frame's list.

parameterdescription.para: Zero-based stack frame index (0 = innermost frame).
Called once for each local variable.

simplesect.para: Must be called while the target is stopped.

memberdef.argsstring: (int frameIndex, int symbolIndex, const std::function< void(const juce::String &name, const juce::String &value, const juce::String &type, bool hasChildren, int symbolIndex)> &function) noexcept
memberdef.name: applyToVariableChildren

param.type: const std::function< void(const juce::String &name, const juce::String &value, const juce::String &type, bool hasChildren, int symbolIndex)> &

briefdescription.para: Calls function for each child of a variable, to expand it in DAP.

detaileddescription.para: Windows calls IDebugSymbolGroup2::ExpandSymbol on the symbol at symbolIndex, then iterates the newly exposed children. macOS reads SBValue::GetNumChildren and GetChildAtIndex directly on the cached parent value. liblldb builds children on demand, with no separate expand step.
function receives the same arguments as in applyToLocals.

parameterdescription.para: Zero-based stack frame index containing the parent variable.
Index of the parent symbol in the frame's symbol list.
Called once for each child.

simplesect.para: Must be called while the target is stopped.

briefdescription.para: Evaluate a C++ expression in the context of a specific stack frame.

detaileddescription.para: Windows gets the frame's symbol group, adds the expression to that group with AddSymbol while SYMOPT_NO_PUBLICS is set, and formats the new symbol. The previous symbol options are restored on exit, and the added symbol is removed from the group. A result is returned only when AddSymbol returns S_OK. macOS calls SBFrame::EvaluateExpression directly on the requested frame and formats the resulting SBValue the same way as applyToLocals. On failure it returns the SBError description, or "evaluation failed" when the error has no text.

parameterdescription.para: C++ expression string to evaluate (e.g. "myVar->field").
Zero-based stack frame index for symbol resolution context.

simplesect.para: Formatted result string. On Windows, an empty string when AddSymbol does not return S_OK.
Must be called while the target is stopped. Complex expressions may cause the engine to execute target code (function calls in expression).

briefdescription.para: Appends the threads of the target process to json, as DAP thread objects.

detaileddescription.para: Windows uses IDebugSystemObjects::GetNumberThreads and GetThreadIdsByIndex to list all threads, and resolves each name with GetThreadDescription. A thread with no description is named "Thread " followed by its id. macOS uses SBProcess::GetNumThreads and GetThreadAtIndex, and reads each SBThread ID and name.

Each appended thread object has these fields:
id (int) — OS thread ID (system TID, not the engine's internal index)
name (String) — thread name; empty on macOS when the thread has none

parameterdescription.para: Output text that receives the thread objects.

simplesect.para: Must be called while the target is stopped.

briefdescription.para: Return the OS thread ID of the thread that triggered the last debug event.

detaileddescription.para: Windows calls IDebugSystemObjects::GetEventThread then GetCurrentThreadSystemId, restoring the previously current thread afterward; valid only immediately after a WaitForEvent call returns an event (i.e., while stopped). macOS reads SBProcess::GetSelectedThread's SBThread ID directly — the stop-reason dispatch in pollEvents already selects the reporting thread.

simplesect.para: OS system thread ID, or 0 if the query fails.

briefdescription.para: Set the current debug context to the thread with the given OS thread ID.

detaileddescription.para: Windows looks up the dbgeng internal thread index for systemId and calls IDebugSystemObjects::SetCurrentThreadId. macOS calls SBProcess::SetSelectedThreadByID directly with systemId. All subsequent symbol queries (applyToLocals, appendStackFrames, evaluateExpression) operate on this thread's context.

parameterdescription.para: OS system thread ID to make current.

simplesect.para: Must be called while the target is stopped. On Windows, an id that dbgeng does not know is ignored, and 0 fails an assert.

briefdescription.para: Discards the cached symbol group (Windows) or the cached frame variables (macOS).

detaileddescription.para: The cache is keyed on frame index, and a stop changes the program counter, so the cache must be discarded. VariableManager::resetVariablesState calls it. shutdown calls it too.

briefdescription.para: Refresh cachedFrameVariables for the given frame if stale.

detaileddescription.para: Mirrors Windows getOrCreateSymbolGroup — keyed on frame index; regenerates the SBValueList when the cached index does not match. Callers may rely on cachedFrameVariables being valid for frameIndex after this returns.

parameterdescription.para: Zero-based stack frame index (0 = innermost).

briefdescription.para: Cross-platform debug engine wrapper used by Processor, BreakpointManager, VariableManager, and StopManager to drive a debug session: launching and attaching processes, polling for events, setting breakpoints, inspecting symbols, and stepping.

detaileddescription.para:
Two independent implementations share this one declaration, selected at compile time by JUCE_WINDOWS / JUCE_MAC:
Windows: COM wrapper around dbgeng (IDebugClient5 and friends).
macOS: wrapper around liblldb's SB API (SBDebugger, SBTarget, SBProcess).

Ownership (Windows):
Owns the Loader that loaded dbgeng.dll.
Owns OutputCallbacks and EventCallbacks registered with IDebugClient5.
Owns all COM interface ComPtrs; releases them in ~Session.

Ownership (macOS):
Owns the SBDebugger, SBListener, SBTarget, and SBProcess instances for the lifetime of the session.

simplesect.para: The engine context runs every method, except wake and cancel. The reader thread calls wake and cancel through Processor::addRequest. On Windows, COM is initialized in multithreaded mode by initialize().
